entry.name: mc.playlist~
entry.digest: Play sound files with multichannel output
entry.description: Use mc.playlist~ to organize sound files and play them back using multichannel outputs. Each file's waveform is shown in a clip where you can select a portion of the file for playback. Drag clips within an mc.playlist~ to re-order them, or drag clips to other mc.playlist~ objects by using the dotted handle on the clip's left edge.

attributes.name: slurtime
attributes.description: Set the time it takes for the correction to reach the full corrected amount. Typically, notes are a bit unstable at the beginning, because the attack phase of a sound has a higher amount of noise, and because singers gradually adjust their tuning after the onset of the note. The slur time makes the pitch correction sound natural because it models this effect. Higher values will yield a slower adaptation time and it will take longer for the correction to produce the corrected pitch. However, longer slur times will also preserve vibrato better.andmust be enabled first.

messages.name: (drag)
messages.description: Create a newobject by dragging and dropping a multichannel audio file into an unlocked patch. To load additional audio files into anobject, drag the new file onto theUI until a line appears above or below the currently loaded file. To rearrange tracks within, click and drag the handle (dot on the left side) up or down in a locked patch. To replace a currently loaded file, drag the new file over the old one until the entire track is highlighted.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Use your mouse to play and stop the playlist, also use it to select small parts of the sample for playback.

messages.name: append
messages.digest: Add a new soundfile to the list
messages.description: Add a new soundfile to the list. First (optional) argument specifies the soundfile. Second (optional) argument specifies the slot number for the clip (starting at 1). If no arguments are listed, clicking the append message in a locked patcher will open a dialog box where you can choose a file to append.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: Remove all clips from the playlist. To remove just one clip, right-click on the file you wish to remove in a locked patcher and choose "Remove" from the contextual menu.

messages.name: getcontent
messages.digest: Get the content and behavior of all clips
messages.description: The wordsends the contents and behavior of all clips out the last outlet ofin dictionary format. Connect the last outlet to aobject to see the contents. Please note that for the "absolutepath" entry, the full file path for each clip will only be displayed if the file is not in Max's search path. If the file is in Max's search path, only the file name will be displayed.

messages.name: int
messages.description: 0 stops soundfile playback. A number greater than zero begins playback of the clip with that index. Indices begin counting at 1.

messages.name: next
messages.description: Plays the next clip loaded in.

messages.name: pause
messages.description: Pause playback of the current clip at the current position.

messages.name: remove
messages.description: The word, followed by a clip number starting at 1, removes that clip from the list.

messages.name: resume
messages.description: Resume playback from the current position if playback has been paused. This message has no effect when using signal-driven playback.

messages.name: selection
messages.digest: Select playback endpoints for a clip
messages.description: Select playback endpoints for a clip using a normalized range (0.0 is the beginning, 1.0 is the end). The first argument specifies which clip (starting at 1). The second argument is the start point for the clip, and the third argument is the end point. If only two arguments are given, they serve as the start and end points for all clips in mc.playlist~. If only one argument is given, it serves as the clip number and clears any selection from that clip.

messages.name: selectionms
messages.digest: Select playback endpoints for a clip in milliseconds
messages.description: Select playback endpoints for a clip in milliseconds. The first argument specifies which clip (starting at 1). The second argument is the start point for the clip, and the third argument is the end point. If only two arguments are given, they serve as the start and end points for all clips in mc.playlist~. If only one argument is given, it serves as the end point for all clips in mc.playlist~.

messages.name: setclip
messages.digest: Set an attribute state for a specific clip
messages.description: attributes are available in mc.playlist~. To control a specific clip, use the "setclip" message followed by the clip number, attribute name, and value. The message "setclip 2 loop 1" will turn looping on for clip 2.

messages.name: signal
messages.digest: Trigger a stored cue with sample accuracy
messages.description: An input signal may be used for the sample-accurate triggering of prestored cues. When a signal value is received in the left inlet, the integer portion of the signal value is monitored. When the integer portion of the input signal changes to a value equal to the index of a prestored cue, that cue is triggered. Indexes start at 1. A signal value of 0 stops audio. Negative values are ignored.

outlets.description: produces a multichannel signal containing the number of channels specified by theattribute.

The second outlet provides a single-channel sync signal. The integer part of the signal value is the index of the clip that is playing. The fractional part is the instantaneous position within that clip.
The third outlet sends the messagefollowed by a clip index and name when a clip starts playing andfollowed by a clip index and name when a clip stops playing.
outputs a dictionary describing its current contents out the right outlet in response to amessage.
